Both settings are optional because the destination is undecided (`KU-14`).
Unset, the api starts normally, records escalations at
`no_destination_configured`, notifies nobody and logs one
`escalation.no_destination` warning at startup. In the chart,

optionally, `token`. The records live in the `escalations` collection, so a
record and its place in the retry schedule survive a restart. A record whose
process died mid-send is claimed again by the next process after 10 minutes, so
the destination may receive it twice.

customer's conversation is `infra/terraform/access/main.tf`; this page explains

read what a customer typed. This page and the terraform root hold work email
addresses, role names and a one-line reason per person, and nothing else.

yet. Until it is, the only member is `user:placeholder@example.com`, and no
real address is committed. Adding the n…

Escalation is a stated product requirement, not a fallback. Kristian's target and anti-target are both explicit: an insurance robot that took too long to admit it needed to transfer him, versus a tax-authority chat that gave up quickly and was a better experience for it - and the intended destination is a phone call, with OLT contacting the customer as soon as the agent can't answer. token counts and how the turn ended, never what anyone wrote. A provider
failover adds a row of its own, with no session or user: the two provider types,
the error code and how long the failed call ran. A tool call that

moves everyone after them to another customer. Set one of the two, never both.

"issue-24" (2026-10-08T23:14:23Z) — 10 section(s):

[1] "issue-24" section 1:
Issue #24 in re-cinq/Otto: Hand a support conversation off to a human when the agent cannot answer
State: closed
Author: gedaiu
Labels: area:compliance, size:M, epic:E4, repo:otto, type:feature, area:api, area:tools, priority:low
Opened: 2026-08-21T08:29:51Z
Closed: 2026-09-21T12:01:22Z
Link: https://github.com/re-cinq/Otto/issues/24

Part of #1

> **Blocked:** Where an escalation lands, and who is on the other end during which hours, is undecided - OLT has no customer support platform and none is planned before step two of their own implementation plan (KU-14, owner Kristian Ladefoged; UU-09, UU-10)

[2] "issue-24" section 2:
## Why

Escalation is a stated product requirement, not a fallback. Kristian's target and anti-target are both explicit: an insurance robot that took too long to admit it needed to transfer him, versus a tax-authority chat that gave up quickly and was a better experience for it - and the intended destination is a phone call, with OLT contacting the customer as soon as the agent can't answer. Nothing in either meeting says *where* an escalation lands, and OLT has no support platform today. `051` already put a hand-off sentence in the prompt with a guarded placeholder channel, `049` made TMS `unavailable`/`timeout` results branchable specifically for this issue, and `003` lists the hand-off as an unmapped destination. This issue builds everything the missing destination doesn't block, and states plainly what it doesn't yet deliver.

[3] "issue-24" section 3:
## What to do

Add `apps/api/src/escalation/`: `triggers.ts` (an `EscalationTrigger` union), `escalationRecorder.ts` (`mark` during a turn, `flush` at the end of it), `escalationSink.ts` (the port - `deliver(record)`), `recordOnlySink.ts` (the only implementation, writing through `053`'s repository into an `escalations` collection and notifying nobody), and `escalationHooks.ts` (flushes via `afterSession`, same rationale as `053`'s write path - it's the one per-turn hook that fires inside a `finally`, so a provider outage still flushes). Add the `escalate_to_human` tool (`apps/api/src/tools/escalateToHuman/tool.ts`) with one required, enum-constrained input `reason_category` (`no_tool_for_question`, `customer_asked_for_human`, `out_of_scope_change_request`).

[4] "issue-24" section 4:
## What to do

Two trigger mechanisms, and neither reads the model's prose: **deterministic** triggers fire from `049`'s factory when a tool call returns `unavailable` or `timeout` (one call site, every tool inherits it); the **model-mediated** trigger is the `escalate_to_human` tool call itself. No code pattern-matches the assistant's Danish output for transfer language - a regex over model text is silently wrong in exactly the case that matters most: a model that says it will transfer the customer with no record created. Since `escalate_to_human` makes no HTTP call and can't fail with a `TmsError`, it can't go through `049`'s factory; add it as a named, literal exemption to that factory's CI grep rather than widening the grep's pattern. The record itself is a pointer, not a copy: `sessionId`, `userId`, `trigger`, `occurredAt`, `updatedAt` - nothing else, since the full conversation is already durable in `053`'s store under its own retention period, and a second copy of the same personal data would need a second retention decision nobody has made. Dedup on `sessionId`: a TMS outage failing every tool call in a conversation produces one escalation record with multiple trigger entries, not one per failed message.

[5] "issue-24" section 5:
## What to do

The customer is told in the same turn, with no retry loop - the hand-off sentence lives in `051`'s prompt module and promises contact, not a time window or a channel, since no source commits to either. Render nothing new in `bowman-ui`: the sentence arrives through the existing `entry_delta`/`entry_commit` path, since a hand-off is the answer to the question just asked and belongs in the transcript, not a toast that auto-dismisses.

[6] "issue-24" section 6:
## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `EscalationTrigger` is a union of `tms_unavailable`, `tms_timeout`, `no_tool_for_question`, `customer_asked_for_human`, `out_of_scope_change_request`; a `switch` over it with no `default` compiles, failing `npm run typecheck` if a trigger is added without a matching case elsewhere
- [ ] A tool call returning `unavailable` or `timeout` marks an escalation with no model action - tested with a mock provider emitting no `escalate_to_human` call, asserting one record exists
- [ ] A `not_found` from the same fixture marks no escalation
- [ ] `escalate_to_human` is registered, declares exactly one required enum-constrained `reason_category`; a call with an invalid value is rejected by `037`'s validation as a readable tool result, not a throw, with a `stream_end`
- [ ] No module under `apps/api/src/` matches the assistant's response text against a string or regex to decide an escalation - enforced by a CI grep over `src/escalation/`, and a test drives a turn whose assistant text claims a transfer while no trigger fired, asserting zero records
- [ ] `049`'s factory-only grep passes with `escalateToHuman/tool.ts` as its single named exemption; adding a second non-factory tool file fails the grep

[7] "issue-24" section 7:
## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Three failing turns in one session produce exactly one document with three entries in its `triggers` array; a fourth turn in a different session produces a second document
- [ ] `flush` empties the pending map even when `deliver` rejects, and the thrown error does not reach the customer as a failed turn
- [ ] **GDPR.** The persisted record has exactly five fields (`sessionId`, `userId`, `trigger`, `occurredAt`, `updatedAt`) - tested against a turn whose message and tool input both carry a name, phone number, and booking reference, asserting none appear anywhere in the stored document
- [ ] **GDPR.** The `escalations` collection is covered by `053`'s retention sweep with the same period; erasing a conversation by `sessionId` erases its escalation record in the same operation
- [ ] **NIS-2.** A TMS outage degrades support rather than stopping it: the turn completes with a `stream_end`, an assistant entry is committed, and the conversation remains usable for a further message
- [ ] **EU AI Act.** `escalate_to_human` performs no TMS call and mutates nothing - zero transport calls, no import from `packages/tms-client`

[8] "issue-24" section 8:
## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The spec's first paragraph states plainly that no human is notified by this issue and names the queued follow-up that delivers the notification; the literal string "notifies nobody" appears in `recordOnlySink.ts`
- [ ] `003`'s data-flow record is updated: the escalation hop stops being an unmapped destination and becomes a named store with a retention period, still recording that the recipient is undecided
- [ ] `npm run build`, `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck` and `npm test` pass at the repo root

[9] "issue-24" section 9:
## Tech notes

Out of scope: delivering the escalation anywhere (an inbox, a queue, a call list - there is none yet; a queued follow-up owns it once `KU-14` closes); tool-budget exhaustion as a trigger (HAL Engine exits its loop silently today with no signal to branch on - two queued `hal-engine` issues); human confirmation before a consequential tool call (E5 - this issue's tools are all read-only); the provider-outage failover path (a different failure with a different response, owned by E5); the ten questions that decide which requests have no tool (`050`, this trigger works without knowing them); any `bowman-ui`/`apps/web` change.

`Toast` (shipped in an earlier issue on the justification that escalation needed it) turns out not to be the right surface - a hand-off is the answer to the question the customer just asked and belongs in the persisted transcript, not a two-second notification; if `Toast`'s remaining justification (provider-outage failover) also declines it, deleting the component before 1.0 is a one-line change. Lore memory: no prior decision found for human escalation, hand-off, or ticketing in the org - no notification transport and no precedent to reuse (`lore-gaps.md` G55).

[10] "issue-24" section 10:
## Tech notes

Build with `/lore-feature "Hand a support conversation off to a human when the agent cannot answer"` - spec lands at `specs/support-agent-human-escalation/spec.md`, tasks at `tasks.md`, description via `/lore-pr`.
